classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied parallel construction to transfer the triangle base angles into a straight-angle proof.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=180^\circ$, that is, prove that the sum of the angles in any triangle is $180^\circ$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20a, triangle beneath the proof instruction at left
spec.description: Triangle DBE has horizontal base DE and apex B above it. Horizontal A–B–C passes through B. Matching rightward parallel chevrons lie on BC and DE. Interior labels alpha, beta and gamma lie at D, B and E. No angle arcs, lengths or numerical measures are supplied.
spec.mathematics: A,B,C are collinear and ABC is parallel to DE. Alpha is angle BDE, beta is angle DBE and gamma is angle BED. Coordinates establish a qualitative triangle only; no numerical dimensions are asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source vertex and Greek angle labels are visible. The proof and alternate-angle equalities are solution-only.

answer.short: $\angle ABD=\alpha$ and $\angle CBE=\gamma$ by alternate angles. Angles on the straight line $ABC$ give $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$ABC\parallel DE$.

$\angle ABD=\alpha$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$\angle CBE=\gamma$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

Consider the straight line $ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABD+\angle DBE+\angle EBC&=180^\circ\\\alpha+\beta+\gamma&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$

Thus the angles in any triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
